note: Language Lab practice settings based on the USCIS scoring guidelines for the reading and writing portions. They are NOT USCIS rules: a text comparison cannot judge pauses, pronunciation or whether an officer understands. See scoringBasis for the source and what each setting stands for.

scoringBasis.source: USCIS Policy Manual, Volume 12, Part E, Chapter 2 (English and Civics Testing), Reading Test and Writing Test
scoringBasis.rule: An attempt counts when every content word of the sentence is present, in order. Short words may be missing or added. A plural or possessive ending is not a different word. A missing or substituted content word does not count. (Guideline: the applicant must read all content words but may omit short words; omitting or substituting a content word fails.)
scoringBasis.functionWordsNote: The manual does not define short words. These are the 'Other (Function)' words of the two official USCIS vocabulary lists in data/sources/ (reading: a, for, here, in, of, on, the, to, we; writing: and, during, for, here, in, of, on, the, to, we).
scoringBasis.extraContentWordsNote: The guidelines do not list an inserted word as a failure, and a speech recogniser can add one, so one extra content word is allowed. More do not count.
scoringBasis.spellingNote: Writing guideline: spelling, capitalization and punctuation errors do not fail unless they interfere with the meaning. A one-letter spelling error in a word of 5 letters or more is accepted (writing only), unless the typed word is itself a different word of the official vocabulary.
